name: Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
history: French priests of the Congregation of the Sacred Hearts arrived in Honolulu in 1827 and said the first recorded Catholic Mass in Hawaii in a grass hut. After years of persecution, King Kamehameha III gave them land from the royal estate. Ground was broken on 9 July 1840, the Feast of Our Lady of Peace, and native Hawaiian volunteers cut coral blocks from the shores of Ala Moana, Kakaʻako and Waikīkī. It was dedicated on 15 August 1843.
arch: Built of coral blocks, with plaster, marble, terra cotta and koa wood. Bishop Maigret built the first domed bell tower in Hawaii, later replaced in 1866 by a wooden spire with a globus cruciger.
features: It is said to be the oldest cathedral in continuous use in the United States, and its clock is the oldest in Hawaii.
A rooster finial on the spire is often mistaken for a weather vane.

look.d: The 1866 spire carries an orb-and-cross and a fixed rooster.
Bishop Maigret bought the tower clock and a larger bell.

fun: St. Damien of Molokai was ordained a priest here in 1864.
journal: Coral cut from Waikīkī's shore, stacked into a cathedral. Aloha and Ave Maria.

quiz.q: What were the walls built from?
